{{Quote|If Nuso Esva isn't stopped, it's the only possible outcome. If he succeeds in holding the Red City, it'll be only a matter of time before he also takes the White City, then the Black City, and then the entire planet.|Stormtrooper [[Lhagva]]|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
'''Quethold''' was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Quethold system/Legends|Quethold system]] of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. The planet, which contained several [[Mining/Legends|mines]], was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Quesoth]] [[Species/Legends|species]], which spoke the [[Quesoth Common Speak]] and [[Quesoth Soldier Speak|Soldier Speak]] [[Language/Legends|languages]]. The Quesoth lived periodically in three [[City/Legends|cities]]: the [[Black City]], the [[Red City]], and the [[White City]]. The three settlements were ruled by three [[Queen of the Quesoth|Queens of the Quesoth]] which changed and [[Death/Legends|died]] once their rule had lasted for a number of [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. The inhabitants of each city then would travel to the next one.

In ancient [[Time/Legends|times]], the Quesoth engaged in a series of wars with the [[Stromma]] species that became known as the latter's [[Expansion Period]]. The Stromma suffered heavy losses, and made peace with the Quesoth, eventually becoming their allies. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], the [[Storm-hair]] [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]] and thirty of [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]], the [[Chosen (Nuso Esva)|Chosen]], arrived at the Red City and Esva allied himself with the ruling [[Queen of the Red (8 ABY)|Queen of the Red]]. Both planned to murder the Queen of the White so the Red monarch could rule Quethold forever while the Storm-hairs could use the White City's [[Starship/Legends|starships]] [[Shipyard/Legends|manufacturing]] facilities to leave Quethold and [[Nuso Esva's conquests|attack]] their enemies. However, the [[Empire of the Hand]] [[Blockade/Legends|blockaded]] Quethold so that Esva could not escape, and [[Attack on the Red City|attacked]] the Red City to eliminate the warlord. Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] sieged [[Quesoth Soldier]]s and Chosen while attacking [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|aircraft]] bombarded Storm-hair [[Stromma cannon|defenses]]. Fearing she was a [[Treason/Legends|traitor]], Esva murdered the Queen of the Red, prompting her Soldiers to kill him.

==Description==
Quethold was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> located in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions']] [[Quethold system/Legends|Quethold system]].<ref name="EAOC-Q" /> The [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Quesoth]] [[Species/Legends|species]] were [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to Quethold. The world featured the [[Dreaming Waters]], a [[Water/Legends|water]] body located to the north of the Red City, and several [[Mining/Legends|mines]].<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==History==
===Nuso Esva's storm===
{{Quote|It was long ago, during the foolish arrogance we called our Expansion Period. Even with the primitive ceremonial weapons they still use, we suffered greatly before we came to our senses and made peace with them.|Stromma Council Liaison Nyama|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
[[File:Jorj.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Former smuggler Jorj Car'das (pictured) suggested Thrawn visit the Quesoth.]]
Long before<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],<ref name="Crisis of FaithD">The events of ''[[Crisis of Faith]]'' take place in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]] according to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.</ref> the [[Stromma]] species engaged in wars against Quethold's Quesoth that were known as the Stromma [[Expansion Period]]. The former suffered significantly before they surrendered and became Quesoth allies. As such, the Stromma were given a residence in the [[Red City]]'s [[Dwelling of Guests]] building.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="ChoicesD">The events of ''[[Choices of One]]'' take place in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] according to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]].</ref> the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Senior Captain]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] [[Battle of the Poln system|confronted]] the<ref name="Choices">''[[Choices of One]]''</ref> [[Storm-hair]]<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Poln system/Legends|Poln system]]. While the Storm-hair's [[Eastern Fleet]] prepared to [[Death/Legends|kill]] Thrawn, Esva revealed what the fate of all his allies was: being tools. The Chiss had anticipated such a comment, and using the [[Comm unit/Legends|comm]] of [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[DeepWater-class light freighter|''DeepWater''-class light freighter]] ''[[Lost Reef]]'', relayed the warlord's comment into the Unknown Regions, where both Quesoth<ref name="Choices" /> and Stromma&mdash;<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> species Esva hoped to "ally" with&mdash;could hear. Esva did not care about them hearing his words, instead attempting to defeat Thrawn's Imperial forces; however, the Galactic Empire's [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]] fleet arrived, shattering Esva's fleet, whose leader fled. In the aftermath of the destruction of the Eastern Fleet, an ally of Thrawn's, former [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Jorj Car'das]], suggested that Thrawn should visit the Quesoth.<ref name="Choices" />

Eight [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, in 8 ABY,<ref name="Crisis of FaithD" /> the Red [[City/Legends|City's]] [[Queen of the Red]] allied herself with the Storm-hair warlord. While the Storm-hair promised to murder the White City's [[Queen of the White]], who would succeed the Red monarch, the Queen of the Red would grant him access to the White City's [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] so that Esva and his thirty [[Chosen (Nuso Esva)|Chosen]] [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]]&mdash;who took the Stromma's place in the Dwelling of Guests after they arrived in Quethold's Red City&mdash;could flee Quethold and [[Nuso Esva's conquests|assault]] their enemies.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

===The approaching storm===
{{Quote|Besides, Nuso Esva isn't going to be leaving Quethold. Not anymore. Certainly not alive.''"<br />"''Liaison Nyama makes a valid point. Wherever his remnant is hiding, Nuso Esva surely has insufficient ships to break through our blockade.|Stromma Council Liaison Nyama and [[Stormtrooper Commander]] [[Balkin]]|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
[[File:Admonitor.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The "star caravan" ''Admonitor'' blockaded Quethold in an attempt to prevent Esva's escape.]]
The [[Empire of the Hand]], which now-[[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] Thrawn led, learnt of Esva's presence on Quethold and saw it as an opportunity to end him and his [[Nuso Esva's realm|realm]] of destruction. [[Blockade/Legends|Blockading]] Quethold with the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Admonitor]]'', the Empire of the Hand ensured Esva could not leave Quethold. One [[Standard month/Legends|month]] after the warlord's arrival, the member of the Quesoth [[Midli]] caste&mdash;which oversaw the [[Workers (Quesoth)|Workers]] caste&mdash;[[Trevik]] became the Queen of the Red's [[bowlcarrier]], carrying a bowl of [[Nectar/Legends|nectar]] from which the monarch [[Diet/Legends|drank]]. Trevik accompanied the Queen's entourage to the Dwelling of Guests, where Esva and the Queen discussed their goal: the destruction of their common enemy, Grand Admiral Thrawn of the First of the Chiss of the Empire of the Hand.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

Over Quethold, aboard the ''Admonitor'', a council of high-ranking members of the Empire of the Hand discussed if and how they would deal with Esva. [[Stromma Council Liaison]] [[Nyama]], who spoke for the Stromma government of the [[Stromma council]], was confident that Esva would not be leaving Quethold alive, and the Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] [[TIE pilot|pilot]] believed they would be strong enough to destroy the [[Quesoth Soldier]]s and Esva's remnant of Chosen; Nyama did not believe they would be. Thrawn required information, and Nyama suggested that they could plant a [[Holocamera/Legends|holocam]] on one of the Quesoth who was displeased with the Quesoth&ndash;Storm-hair alliance. The Chiss thought that if the Quesoth could record the [[Painting/Legends|artwork]] Esva had surrounded himself with in the Dwelling of Guests, he would know that the Storm-hair's tactics would be in the upcoming engagement.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

Unbeknownst to any Imperial, Nyama was a [[Treason/Legends|traitor]] who was working for the Queen of the Red and indirectly for Esva. The Stromma Council Liaison had been instructed to make Thrawn think that the artwork indeed represented Esva's tactics although they did not, as the paintings had been picked by the warlord just to confuse the Grand Admiral. Trevik's [[Trevik's family|brother]], [[Jirvin]], had one of the Queen of the Red's advisors and [[Reproduction/Legends|breeders]], a [[Circling]], intercept the bowlcarrier on his way [[Trevik's home|home]] that [[Standard day/Legends|night]]. The Circling brought Trevik to Jirvin, who instructed him with recording Esva's artwork. The bowlcarrier did as ordered, and the [[attack on the Red City]] was programmed to happen the next day at midmorning.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

===End of the old ways===
{{Dialogue|Queen of the Red|The old ways are at an end, Trevik of the Midli of the Seventh of the Red. Why should I accept death for myself and my city merely because the Queen of the White has arisen?|Trevik|But- But the old Queen always dies when the new Queen arises and the air changes. It's the way of the world.|Warlord Nuso Esva|You're a naïve fool. A Queen-a true Queen-doesn't simply sit back and accept the way of the world. A true Queen grasps the world by the throat and squeezes her own destiny from it. Understand?|attr=The Queen of the Red, bowlcarrier Trevik, and Warlord Nuso Esva|src=<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
Nyama, who gave the recordings to Thrawn, also translated several of the Queen of the Red's orders spoken in [[Quesoth Soldier Speak]], which the Grand Admiral recorded. Esva prepared his defenses, with his Storm-hairs commandeering the [[Stromma cannon]]s in the Red City to use them as defenses against the Imperial fighters. The warlord, the Queen, and her bowlcarrier then met in the Dwelling of Guests, where the allies prepared to lead the Quesoth and Storm-hair sides of the battle. Thrawn sent nine [[juggernaut]]s along the City's [[Setting Sun Avenue]] and several [[Transport/Legends|transports]] in the settlement's outskirts. Empire of the Hand [[A-rack]]s carried three [[Squadron/Legends|squads]] of stormtroopers while TIE fighters [[Scout/Legends|scouted]] for the Chosen and their defenses, several of which were hidden in the homes of the Quesoth Workers and Midlis.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

[[File:ChosenNusoEsva.png|thumb|right|300px|The Chosen (pictured) fought the Imperial stormtroopers on Quethold.]]
Nearly four thousand Quesoth sieged the stormtroopers, reaching the nine juggernauts in an attempt to capture them to use them in the siege of the White City; however, the Chosen discovered that the vehicles were empty, driven by [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and equipped with no [[Weapon/Legends|weaponry]]. The TIEs destroyed the [[Speaker/Legends|speakers]] transmitting the Queen of the Red's commands to the Quesoth Soldiers while Imperial [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]] used one to transmit a command in Quesoth Soldier Speak: "''Go through the Dwelling doors. Surround and protect the Guests.''" Esva did not know what the command was ordering the Soldiers to do, and seeing them rushing to enter the Dwelling of Guests, feared that the Queen was a traitor, killing her. The warlord killed all Quesoth present but Trevik, who he tasked with delivering a message that warned Thrawn that although Esva was dead, his followers would find the Chiss, wherever he tried to hide, and kill him. The Storm-hair was then killed by the Soldiers and the Chosen died as a result of the stormtroopers' laser fire.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

As the Red City had been damaged during the attack, the Empire of the Hand had seized Quethold and offered assistance in rebuilding it. The empire's leader, Thrawn, believed that the Chosen were too scattered and too few to ever be a threat without Esva, dismissing the threat. Shortly after, the ''Admonitor'' left for the [[Chaos Triangle]], where it was to cleanup what Thrawn referred to as Esva's "legacy."<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Inhabitants==
The inhabitants of Quethold, the Quesoth, were divided in three castes. The Circling caste was made of breeders and advisors of great quality; the Quesoth Soldiers fought; the Midli caste oversaw the Workers. The [[Queen of the Black]] ruled the [[Black City]], the Red City was under the rule of the Queen of the Red, and the [[White City]] was ruled by the White monarch, the Queen of the White. The Quesoth lived in one of the cities until a city's ruler had ruled for a number of years, when the monarch would die in the process known as the "changing of air" and the settlement's inhabitants would travel to the next city. The Quesoth spoke the [[Quesoth Common Speak]] and Soldier Speak&mdash;which could only be spoken by the Soldiers and their [[Queen of the Quesoth|Queen]]&mdash;[[Language/Legends|tongues]].<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Locations==
The Black, Red, and White cities were all located on Quethold. The Red City contained a [[Palace (Red City)|palace]], several Midli, Worker, and Soldier homes, as well as the Dwelling of Guests. The [[Stromma diplomatic enclave]] was located at the edge of the Black City.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Behind the scenes==
Quethold first appeared in the novella ''[[Crisis of Faith]]'', written by [[Timothy Zahn]] and published in [[2011]] as part of the [[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition|20th Anniversary Edition]] of the [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]''.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />
